nina: Quick sync — Lighthouse (large eds customer) pushed back: they want predictable burst economics and a clear canary plan before GA. Asking for a written fallback if burst drains >50% of monthly budget.

ash: Understood. We need to be concrete: what is the burst primitive we ship for GA? Token-bucket? Fixed short-term autoscale? micro-pools?

leo: Ops input: token-bucket + escrow looks fastest. We can implement per-tenant escrowed credits that draw from a monthly allotment. Runtime will enforce bucket checks at admission time.

clare: Sales/legal note: customers want an explicit "buyback" option — if they hit burst and want to refund credits because of perceived poor quality, we need refund rules in the contract. Also they want a 1-hour rollback window for any forced throttle.

nina: Can we codify default GA parameters? Proposal: baseline = committed GPUs X (set at sign), burst multiplier = 4x, burst window = 10 minutes, monthly burst budget = 12 windows (i.e., 120 minutes). Escrow draws from budget.

ash: Quick math for sizing: if baseline capacity = 10 GPUs, multiplier 4x -> provisional burst capacity = 30 extra GPUs for 10 minutes. Token-bucket capacity = extra_gpus * window_seconds = 30 * 600 = 18000 gpu-seconds. We'll expose those as "credit-seconds" in UI.

leo: Runtime details: admission check = if tenant.credit_seconds_remaining >= request.estimated_gpu_seconds then allow, else reject or queue. We should also support a "soft-allow" where we allow but mark for preemption earlier.

clare: Contract language idea (short): "Provider offers reserved capacity as committed GPUs. Provider grants monthly burst credits (in gpu-minutes). When credits exhausted, Provider may throttle or preempt according to documented preemption order. Customers may request a one-time credit appeal within 24h of event for possible buyback per dispute policy."

nina: Canary plan: start with feature flag, 2 pilot tenants, canary ramp 1% -> 5% -> 20% traffic over 48h windows. Canary checks: per-tenant p95 latency, error rate, preemption events, and cost delta. Abort on: p95 increase >30% or error rate >0.5% increase.

ash: Tests we need before canary: synthetic spike harness that simulates 8x baseline for 15m (to test exhaustion), and a CHAOS test that preempts opportunistic instances. QA-bot: can you attach test matrix?

qa-bot: Test matrix attached: scenarios = [steady baseline, 3x burst 10m, 5x burst 15m, exhausted budget recovery]. Metrics collected: admission decisions, queue times, preempt_time, token_draws, billing math.

leo: Billing note: convert gpu-seconds to billable units (tokens -> dollars) at contract rate. Need to expose estimated spike cost in the console before admitting a burst that would exceed the soft cap. Implement spend-estimate API that uses recent model perf to estimate token/sec -> gpu-seconds -> cost.

clare: For "no noisy neighbors" ask: we decline isolated micro-pools for GA unless the customer upsells to dedicated private. For GA we'll promise spillover isolation semantics: reserved workloads run on pinned instances with a minimal isolation cushion; burst runs on shared pool with preemption order defined.

nina: Gating checklist for GA (draft):
- contract clause for burst budget, exhaustion, buyback dispute flow (legal sign-off)
- runtime: token-bucket + escrow implementation + spend-estimate API
- telemetry: per-tenant credit_seconds, admission logs, preemption traces, cost projections
- tests: synthetic harness + chaos + regression suite (see QA matrix)
- canary: 2 pilots then staged rollout with feature flag and abort criteria
- customer docs: examples, cost calculator, rollback/resolution flows

ash: Engineering tickets (brief):
- RB-1: token-bucket runtime + escrow ledger + admission API
- RB-2: preemption priority signal + graceful drain hook (30s grace)
- RB-3: spend-estimate API + console prompt for expensive bursts
- RB-4: telemetry docs + per-tenant dashboards + alerts
- RB-5: feature-flag + canary rollout automation

clare: Commercial ask: include soft-cap defn — default soft-cap = 2x monthly baseline spend. If estimated spend > soft-cap, console prompts and auto-throttle unless customer opts-in. Contract to allow customer to raise cap with 7d notice.

nina: Decision items for this thread: 
1) Approve GA params (multiplier=4, window=10m, monthly windows=12) or modify?
2) Approve shared-pool-with-escrow vs micro-pools?
3) Approve canary plan and abort criteria?

leo: My votes: 1) +1 with multiplier=4 but cap ability to change per-customer; 2) shared-pool-with-escrow + clear preempt order; 3) +1 canary 1/5/20% with abort rules.

ash: +1 all. Also add automated alert to sales when a tenant consumes >75% of monthly burst budget.

clare: +1 to all, but require legal to sign off on buyback language before pilot.

nina: Great. Action items: 
- nina + ash: produce exact prod config + cost calc by EOD tomorrow
- leo: runtime ticket drafts by EOD today (RB-1, RB-2)
- clare: draft contract clause + buyback policy + send to legal by Thu
- qa-bot: run synthetic harness once RB-1 lands, report back

qa-bot: reminder: add regression for model-level variance in cost estimate (some models use more GPU time).

nina: Thanks team — we'll record this as GA baseline and surface as 'reserved+burst (escrowed) v1'. Reconvene Fri for signoffs. :rocket:
